One panel of 46,167 instrument-sessions (34 instruments, Oct 2017 to Dec 2022; 9,527 on the 7 USD majors with the dollar share), every input known before the session: σ position (percentile of σ in its last 252 sessions), forecast error, C.OG's turbulent regime, own and market-wide bursts the session before, and the dollar share. Outcomes: the session range and a 1σ stop from the open on the M1 bid/ask path. 2023 onward is not looked at.

The layers are mostly separate inputs, not one thing measured several ways: 9 outputs behave like 5.3 independent ones (8.8 if shifted out of time with each other, 1 if one thing). The overlap is all on the σ side: σ position and σ vs long-run correlate 0.97, P(high regime) 0.67 with σ. Error, bursts and the dollar share sit near 0 with everything.

And they add: out of sample (2019-2022) all five together remove 6.9% of the squared error of the log range against 6.7% for the sum of each alone, and 4.1% vs 4.1% for the stop. Forecast error does most (4.0%), then σ position (2.4%, the over-reaction), regime 0.2%, market-wide burst 0.1%, own burst ~0. The dollar share makes the forecast worse out of sample (−0.3%): it describes risk, it does not move the range.

No pair interacts beyond adding. Of 15 pairs, 3 beat their own shuffled product on the range and 2 on the stop, about what chance gives; the largest gain is +0.08% of squared error with an interval across 0. Regime × dollar share overfits (−0.5 to −0.8%). Across 174 cells, 3 pass Benjamini-Hochberg (0.3 expected false), and none is an interaction: they are the error alone in calm (+6.1pp stop hits, top vs bottom third) and turbulent regimes (+4.9pp), and the London-open timing.

The best-looking pair, σ position × market-wide burst yesterday (+3.2pp on the stop [−0.2, +6.1]), is too noisy to tell and fails Lesson 01: one session more delay flips it to −2.5pp, a 3-session burst look-back gives −0.1pp, 2018 and 2020 and the indices go the other way.

Agreement matters because the layers add: when 3+ point loud and none quiet the 1σ bid/ask stop is hit 42% of the time (n=326, range 1.91σ); when they agree quiet, 22% (1.29σ); when they disagree, 30% (1.55σ), against 32% for all sessions and 29% on mid (the spread adds about 3pp).

C.OG's regime: 95 turbulent episodes, median 63 sessions, 15% of sessions. The error's effect holds across both regimes; no layer pair changes inside the regime beyond noise. Stops are first touched most in the 13-16 London overlap.

For the system: size and stop width can take the layers as a sum (σ × error feedback × an over-reaction haircut, plus a small burst add-on), with no product terms. Product terms are where the overfitting lives.
